title: B-tree requested page reserve reporting

scope.rationale: sqlite3BtreeGetRequestedReserve reports the larger of the live page-format reserve and the latest file-control reserve request so reserve reporting can grow but never shrink below on-disk requirements.

external_source_responsibilities: B-tree serialization and RESERVE_BYTES request publication
dependencies.caller_closure: The complete max-selection body is assigned; file-control request integration remains open.

inputs: Btree with live reserved bytes and latest requested reserve bytes
outputs: Maximum of live and requested reserve
contracts.state_and_results: Pure observation; requested reserve never lowers the reported live reserve.
contracts.locks_callbacks_io: The simplified Btree owner requires caller serialization; no callbacks or I/O.
contracts.failure_and_continuation: Total for valid Btree state and has no error result.

representation_differences: The Zig Btree model stores live reserve directly instead of recomputing pageSize-usableSize.
Caller serialization represents sqlite3BtreeEnter/Leave until the simplified Btree owner gains the native shared-cache mutex boundary.

oracle.protocol: Set requested reserve below and above the live reserve and compare both results.
oracle.normalization: Byte counts are exact; lock events remain pending.

assurance.malformed_input: Invalid Btree ownership is outside the source contract.
assurance.continuation: Observation does not mutate Btree state.

integration.native_call_path: Typed state owner and unit trace exist; file-control caller integration remains pending.

independent_review.notes: Requires file-control and locking integration, pinned-C trace, assurance closure, and independent review.

implementation_spans: Project file-control reserve paths were searched
callers: Unit trace invokes the owner directly
assertions_branches_cleanup: Both active return/conditional blocks are assigned
upstream_tests: Upstream reserve-byte, page-size, codec-extension, and file-control tests cover this owner
Project unit trace covers both maximum branches
